_note: The precise voice of each character for VoiceDesign: what the voice IS (sex, age, accent, pitch, timbre, pace, how sentences end), so fewer voices fit it and it drifts less from line to line. Written from each roster profile's voice; Pitch is measured, not guessed (median F0): an adult woman speaks near 200 Hz, an adult man near 100-150. The first wording put Heather at 287 Hz ('like a kid', the user) and Owen at 279 Hz, so both now say adult, low and mature outright, and Owen's crack is only on a big moment. tools/td-vo-render.py --profiles uses these in place of the script's short description.
Heather: Adult woman in her early twenties, General American accent. A low-to-medium, mature, grown-up voice with a full, rich tone: never childlike, girlish, squeaky or high-pitched. Polished and slightly nasal. Fast, clipped, precise speech with crisp consonants; sentences end on a firm downward note, dismissive and superior. Confident, cold and condescending; sugary only when she is faking it.
Owen: Adult man in his early twenties, General American accent, a big heavy-set guy. A deep, low-pitched bass-baritone voice, warm, round and chesty with a slightly breathy, gravelly edge: a grown man's voice that stays low even when he is excited. Loud, fast and enthusiastic, words tumbling out; only at a real shock does it crack upward for a moment. Goofy, open and good-natured, often on the edge of laughing.
Gwen: Female, 18 years old, General American accent. Low alto for a young woman, slightly husky and smooth. Slow, even, unhurried pace; flat deadpan intonation with very little pitch movement, sentences ending low. Dry and sarcastic, bored with everyone; only softer and warmer when she means it.
Duncan: Adult man in his early twenties, General American accent. A low baritone with a gravelly, raspy edge, like he has been up all night. A lazy, smug drawl: unhurried, words half-mumbled, a smirk you can hear. Sentences trail off low and flat. Tough, sarcastic and teasing; when he means something it drops quieter, never louder.
Courtney: Adult woman in her early twenties, General American accent. A medium-pitched, mature, clear and crisp voice with a tense, tight edge: never childlike, girlish or shrill. Fast, precise, over-articulated speech, every consonant hit, sentences ending sharply like commands. Controlled and bossy; when crossed she gets louder and harsher, the pitch staying where it is.
Izzy: Adult woman in her early twenties, General American accent. A medium-pitched, slightly raspy, grown-up voice: wild but never childlike or squeaky. Manic and fast, sudden whispers then sudden shouts, giggles breaking through, the rhythm all over the place rather than the pitch. Gleeful, fearless and a little unhinged.
Cody: Adult man in his early twenties, General American accent. A light, slightly nasal tenor: a grown man with a youthful, eager sound. Quick and chatty with a nervous little laugh, voice lifting hopefully at the end of sentences. Earnest, plucky and a bit awkward, trying to sound smoother than he is.
Sierra: Adult woman in her early twenties, General American accent. A medium-pitched, breathy, grown-up voice: never childlike, girlish or squeaky. Talks extremely fast in long run-on bursts, barely pausing for breath, excitement building in speed and volume rather than pitch. Intense, overwhelming and adoring, with no off switch.
Lindsay: Adult woman in her early twenties, General American accent. A soft, sweet, airy medium-low voice, warm and a little breathy: a grown woman, never childlike or squeaky. Relaxed, slightly slow, with a dreamy valley-girl lilt and gentle upward endings. Friendly, bubbly and confused, never mean.
Harold: Adult man in his early twenties, General American accent. A nasal tenor with a nerdy, pinched sound. Over-enunciated and fussy, pronouncing words very precisely, pompous when bragging; his voice cracks up into a squeak when he is offended or flustered. Dramatic, earnest and easily wounded.
Leshawna: Adult woman in her early twenties, Black Canadian. A rich, full, warm low-medium voice with big projection, carrying across a room. Confident and rhythmic, punchy emphasis on the key words, a knowing laugh in it. Bold, direct and loyal; she never sounds unsure.
Noah: Adult man in his early twenties, General American accent. A medium baritone, dry and dull on purpose: flat, bored deadpan with almost no pitch movement. Unhurried, crisp diction, a small sigh before answering. Cutting and sarcastic, too lazy to raise his voice.
Bridgette: Adult woman in her early twenties, General American accent. A relaxed, mellow medium voice with a light husky warmth, a laid-back surfer cadence. Calm, easy pace, soft gentle endings; flustered and halting when she has to be harsh. Kind, peacemaking and sincere.
Geoff: Adult man in his early twenties, General American accent. A warm, easygoing medium baritone, a little hoarse from partying. Laid-back 'dude' drawl, relaxed pace, loose and friendly, lifting up excitedly when he cheers. Good-natured and chill, never sharp.
Trent: Adult man in his early twenties, General American accent. A soft, warm, smooth baritone, the voice of a musician. Gentle, even and earnest, an easy rhythm, sincere sentences ending softly; when hurt it goes quiet and plain rather than loud. Calm, kind and honest.
Alejandro: Adult man in his mid twenties with a light Spanish accent. A smooth, velvety low baritone, rich and polished. Slow, deliberate, honeyed delivery, every compliment savoured; charming and seductive on the surface with a cold, controlled edge underneath. Never rushed, never loud.
Chris: Adult man in his late thirties, General American accent: a reality-show host. A low, polished announcer baritone, resonant and smooth, with big projection that stays deep. Punchy showbiz timing and a smug grin in every line. Teasing, delighted by other people's misery, landing the last word of each sentence like a punchline.
